subject: Term adjustment request + usage & performance synthesis
messages:
From: Julie Tan <julie.tan@openretail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion + request for usage & perf summary

Hi Hannah,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for Redwood is coming up on Sept 1 and the leadership team asked me to pull together a concise packet showing: total token spend YTD, perceived latency/availability impacts on our customer flows (esp. checkout chat), and a short ROI blurb that justifies the proposed uplift to the committed tier.

We’ve seen a steady uptick in traffic since the marketing push in May, so procurement is asking whether there’s room to shift to a 12-month term with a 15% uplift in committed tokens in exchange for smoother pricing. Two asks from our side:
- Can you provide a compact usage and perf summary by 08/06?
- If possible, include a short note on expected per-token cost change if we increase the commit vs staying on run-rate.

Cc’ing our procurement lead (procurement@openretail.com) — they’ll handle the legal side once we have high-level econs.

Thanks,
Julie
Julie Tan
Head of Product
OpenRetail

Attachments: none
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Tan <julie.tan@openretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + request for usage & perf summary

Hi Julie — thanks for the note and context. I pulled together a short packet (attached) that covers: token consumption by model & route, 90th/95th percentile server-side latency for your chat endpoints, and a simple cost comparison (run-rate vs 12mo commit + 15% uplift). High-level takeaways:

- Token spend (YTD): 42.1M tokens (70% inference, 30% embeddings/search).
- Peak weekday 95p latency: 410ms on average for the checkout chat route; 99p spikes tied to batched async jobs.
- Run-rate unit cost today: $0.00012/token. Proposed 12mo commit + 15% uplift estimate: $0.000095/token (approx 21% unit saving).

I also included an appendix with a small ROI example assuming your checkout flow converts at 2.3% and an LTV uplift of $2.50 per successful chat-assisted purchase — quick math suggests the commit saves you ~$8.6k/mo at current volume versus run-rate, and puts headroom for 20–30% traffic growth without moving tiers.

Attachments: openretail-q2-usage-report.pdf, latency-sla-snapshot-2026-07.xlsx, proposed-term-amendment-2026-08.docx

Next steps I recommend:
1) Ops review with Ben to validate the latency mitigation plan for peak windows.
2) If procurement is comfortable, confirm target effective unit price and I’ll loop Legal to produce an amendment.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call today if useful.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Julie Tan <julie.tan@openretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + request for usage & perf summary

Julie / Hannah — quick ops note after reviewing the latency snapshot:

- Root cause for 99p spikes: four scheduled batch image-embedding jobs overlap with peak chat traffic between 15:30–16:15 PDT. We can shift those jobs by 90 minutes and enable a temporary autoscale policy during the 2-week post-marketing window to shave 99p from ~720ms to ~420ms.
- Capacity impact: moving to the 15% higher commit gives you consistent headroom for sustained throughput and reduces queuing; I estimate we can eliminate the majority of the spikes for ~$2.4k/mo additional cost net of the unit discounts in the amendment.

I added a short ops runbook to the Drive link (see HubSpot:HS-4527) outlining the job-shift, autoscale guardrails, and a rollback plan. If you want, we can pilot the schedule change this week and monitor for two business days.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ops-runbook-stub.txt (referenced in Drive)
From: Julie Tan <julie.tan@openretail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@openretail.com, Matt Olsen <matt.olsen@openretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + request for usage & perf summary

Thanks, Hannah & Ben — this is super helpful and exactly what we needed. Procurement is okay to proceed on a 12-month amendment at the price point you proposed; they want a short call with Legal to confirm language and the effective date.

Next steps from OpenRetail:
- Procurement (procurement@openretail.com) will send a non-binding purchase intent by EOD tomorrow.
- Matt (ops) will coordinate the pilot schedule change with Ben — Matt, can you pick 2 windows tomorrow?

Hannah — please loop Legal on the amendment and send a one-page summary of the econs for our CFO. Monica, can you draft the amendment covering commit size, unit price, effective date Sept 1 and a 30-day termination notice?

I’ll wait for the procurement note and we can lock in the brief call.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Julie
